office_does: A Seattle City Councilmember votes on the city budget, taxes, zoning and city laws and oversees city departments including police and transportation; this seat is for a one-year unexpired term.
race_blurb: Two first-time candidates are running for the North Seattle seat vacated in 2025: FairVote Washington's Nilu Jenks, who took 54% in the primary, and educator and community-bank co-founder Julie Kang, who took 33%. They differ most on Aurora Avenue enforcement tools, surveillance cameras and taxes.

candidates.summary: Political and Partnerships Director at FairVote Washington and Lake City parent; endorsed by King County Democrats, multiple unions and four sitting councilmembers.
highlights: Proposes 1,000 new affordable housing units in District 5 and backs denser housing near transit [S3][S7]
Supports a 24/7 CARE Department, a community court and violence intervention; opposes SOAP and CCTV expansion while supporting a 1,200-officer target [S3][S5][S6]
Favors progressive revenue, including a proposed tax on AI data centers [S6][S7]
Listed as opposing initiatives I-001 and I-638 [S11]

taxes.basis: Reported to support progressive revenue restructuring and proposed a new tax on AI data centers; no broader tax platform on her site.

spending.basis: Platform proposes new or expanded programs (fully funded 24/7 CARE Department, free transit for all students, 1,000 affordable units) without a restraint or audit plank.

housing.basis: Affordable-housing unit target built through public land and nonprofit partnerships, plus rent stabilization, just-cause eviction and tenant right to counsel.

safety.basis: Leads with CARE Department, community court and violence intervention and opposes SOAP and camera expansion, while also supporting a 1,200-officer target and a North Seattle precinct.

climate.basis: Pledges to 'move us toward meeting our climate goals' and is described as a climate advocate who ties density and transit to climate goals.

experience.basis: Has not held elected office; brings advocacy and political-organizing experience and a prior run for this seat.

reform.basis: Works professionally on voting reform at FairVote Washington and lists implementing ranked-choice voting in 2027 as a priority.

candidates.summary: Seattle University director and faculty member, 30-year District 5 resident, and co-founder of a community bank; endorsed by the Seattle Times in the primary and by the 32nd LD Democrats.
highlights: Supports rebuilding SPD staffing, a second District 5 precinct, the SOAP zone on Aurora and public-safety cameras, alongside on-demand addiction treatment [S3][S5][S6]
Opposes new taxes on residents and says the city imposes a 'heavy financial burden' through rising taxes [S3][S7]
Would shorten permit review and fund affordable housing from JumpStart revenue instead of MHA fees [S3]
Changed her position on public-safety cameras during the campaign, from opposed to supportive with safeguards [S5][S6]
Listed as opposing initiatives I-001 and I-638 [S10]

taxes.basis: Opposes new taxes on residents and criticizes 'rising taxes' and 'another regressive sales tax hike'; supported the city's transit measure while raising concerns about its sales-tax impact, so not a full tax-cut position.

spending.basis: Emphasizes return on investment before new revenue and budgeting for infrastructure within existing means.

housing.basis: Housing plan leads with faster permitting and mixed-income housing near transit and calls MHA 'a tax on desperately needed housing,' while still directing JumpStart revenue to affordable housing.

safety.basis: Supports police staffing, a second precinct, SOAP, cameras and shutting open-air drug markets, paired with on-demand voluntary treatment and CARE coordination.

experience.basis: Has not held elected office; brings education, banking and commission experience.
